codes.label: Post-contract continuity
codes.definition: What happens when a fixed-term, single-client contract ends: whether it can be renewed, extended or turned into a retainer or referrals, and whether a replacement pipeline exists so income doesn't stop.

codes.label: Contract annualization trap
codes.definition: A short fixed-term contract's headline value annualizes to a salary-like figure only if the work renews, so it should not be treated as equivalent to recurring annual income.

codes.label: Single-client concentration risk
codes.definition: Relying on one client (or one major relationship) for most income exposes her to delayed payment, reduced scope, early cancellation or the client's own financial trouble.

codes.label: Contract terms and payment timing
codes.definition: The specifics of the engagement, such as payment schedule, scope, kill fees, IP ownership, exclusivity and termination clauses, determine how secure and usable the money really is.

codes.label: Net income after self-employment costs
codes.definition: Gross contract or business revenue must be reduced by self-employment tax, quarterly estimated taxes, overhead, software, equipment and unbilled time before comparing it to a salary.

codes.label: Replacement health insurance cost
codes.definition: Losing employer-sponsored health coverage means pricing COBRA, marketplace or private plans (for a family, where relevant), a large hidden cost that can erode the income gain and may shift with household income and subsidies.

codes.label: Retirement savings and lost employer match
codes.definition: Leaving means losing employer retirement contributions, matching, vesting or pension value and requires self-funding retirement from less certain income.

codes.label: Paid leave, disability and life coverage
codes.definition: Self-employment removes paid time off, sick leave and group disability or life insurance, so income stops during illness, injury or vacation unless replacement coverage is bought.

codes.label: Savings runway adequacy
codes.definition: Whether existing savings truly cover living costs plus taxes, insurance, business expenses and late payments through a slow or income-free stretch, and how fast the buffer would erode in a worst case.

codes.label: Startup capital and financing
codes.definition: The upfront cost of vehicle, tools and insurance must be funded from savings, loans or equipment financing, with attention to debt payments, cost overruns and what cash reserve remains afterward.

codes.label: Equipment depreciation and upkeep
codes.definition: Vehicles and tools lose value and need maintenance and eventual replacement, so startup spending is an ongoing cost rather than a one-time outlay.

codes.label: Income volatility and ramp-up
codes.definition: Replacing a steady salary with irregular, seasonal or cyclical earnings means a slow first year or two, so a conservative revenue scenario and a plan for lean months are needed.

codes.label: Receivables lag and cash-flow timing
codes.definition: Customers often pay 30 to 90 days late while materials, fuel, loans and taxes are due upfront, so cash-flow timing can strain finances even when work is steady.

codes.label: Moonlighting rule and employment-agreement conflict
codes.definition: Her employer's same-industry moonlighting restriction may already cover her current side work or the new contract, so she must check the exact scope and the risk of termination or reputational damage before acting.

codes.label: Possible waiver or exception from employer
codes.definition: She could ask the employer for a written waiver, exception or sanctioned side arrangement as a way to resolve a policy conflict without quitting.

codes.label: Non-compete and customer non-solicitation limits
codes.definition: His employment agreement or local law may bar him from soliciting or serving his employer's customers, exposing him to lawsuits that could outweigh any gain.

codes.label: Reliability of customer promises
codes.definition: Verbal assurances that customers will follow him are weak evidence and often shrink once price and convenience are compared, so they should be converted to written commitments, deposits or trial jobs before resigning.

codes.label: Liability, insurance and personal asset exposure
codes.definition: A solo operator is personally exposed to accidents, property damage and code violations, so general liability, workers' compensation or its alternatives, and entity structure (such as an LLC) matter for protecting family assets.

codes.label: Licensing, bonding and permit requirements
codes.definition: He must confirm his license allows independent operation and account for any business entity, bonding, supervising qualifier, permit or registration requirements that add cost or delay.

codes.label: Business administration skills and workload
codes.definition: Running a business adds estimating, bidding, invoicing, collections, bookkeeping, marketing, scheduling and taxes, and she or he must honestly assess having and wanting those skills versus the craft itself.

codes.label: Pricing, competition and billable hours
codes.definition: Realistic income depends on local rates, competitor pricing, demand, and the share of hours that are actually billable after estimating, travel and admin.

codes.label: Physical sustainability and injury risk
codes.definition: Solo trade work is physically demanding, and his body is the business's only asset, so long-term capacity to keep working and the cost of an injury stopping all revenue must be weighed.

codes.label: College costs overlapping business ramp-up
codes.definition: The oldest child's tuition arrives in two years just as business income is least predictable, and business income and assets may also change financial aid eligibility.

codes.label: Spouse's income and household buy-in
codes.definition: His wife's part-time income, her ability to increase hours, her role in the business and the family's shared risk tolerance shape how much risk the household can absorb.

codes.label: Career capital and trajectory at current employer
codes.definition: Leaving a senior role means giving up title, mentorship, brand-name projects, network, promotion path and seniority benefits, and may complicate returning to salaried work later.

codes.label: Reputation, references and exit handling
codes.definition: How and when she leaves (notice, timing, relationships with the agency and clients) affects references and future referrals in a small professional community.

codes.label: Independence goals, risk tolerance and fit
codes.definition: Beyond money, the decision depends on whether she or he actually wants autonomy and the day-to-day reality of running a business, tolerance for uncertainty, and whether this is moving toward a goal rather than escaping a frustration.

codes.label: Existing freelance demand as evidence
codes.definition: Her current freelance income shows some independent client demand that makes the path more plausible, though its size, stability and dependence on the employer's name limit how far it proves she can replace a salary.

codes.label: Downside tolerance from age and dependents
codes.definition: Personal circumstances such as age, lack of or presence of dependents and time to recover determine how survivable a failed attempt would be.

codes.label: Phased or hybrid alternatives
codes.definition: Options such as part-time or leave arrangements, building clients on evenings and weekends, or negotiating with the current employer let the person test demand while keeping salary and benefits, instead of an all-or-nothing leap.

codes.label: Fallback plan and exit triggers
codes.definition: Deciding in advance a financial threshold or date for reassessing, and whether re-employment (including rehire by the former employer) is feasible, defines how the move can be reversed if it struggles.

codes.label: Professional isolation and skill development
codes.definition: Working alone removes critique, mentorship and peer feedback, while new clients may also sharpen skills, affecting long-term craft growth.

codes.label: Timing relative to savings and contract start
codes.definition: Whether to decide now while savings are intact or later from a weaker position, and how the contract start date lines up with notice at the current job.

codes.label: Existing freelance clients' reaction to full-time switch
codes.definition: Smaller current clients may stay, expand or leave once she is fully independent, and how that base is maintained affects overall income.

codes.label: Time diverted to marketing and pipeline building
codes.definition: A large engagement or admin load can leave little time to market and nurture new clients, slowing future income growth.

codes.label: Market timing and niche outlook
codes.definition: Freelance demand in her specialty shifts with AI tooling, client budgets and agency consolidation, so the direction of her niche over the contract window may make the move better or worse than her current read suggests.

codes.label: Ownership of past work and portfolio rights
codes.definition: The employer may own the intellectual property of work produced during employment, which can limit her ability to show or reuse those pieces when pitching independent clients.

codes.label: Compounding ownership of independent assets
codes.definition: Independent work builds assets she owns, such as client relationships, pricing power and portfolio rights, which can appreciate over time in ways a fixed salary does not.

codes.label: Dormant projects and untapped skills
codes.definition: Unused portfolio pieces, half-finished side ideas and stored-away skills are an inventory worth taking stock of, since the greatest value of leaving may be the work she has been postponing rather than the immediate contract.

codes.label: Unlisted employer benefits and subsidies
codes.definition: Beyond salary and health premiums, the employer supplies hard-to-see value such as paid training, bonding, overflow work and brand reputation that never appear as a paycheck line item and must be replaced or priced.

codes.label: Referral network as the real asset
codes.definition: His existing trust and referral network is the true source of leverage, and equipment and a vehicle only pay off if they connect that network to paying work, so the plan should be anchored there.

codes.label: Loan and mortgage qualification with self-employment income
codes.definition: Self-employed income is harder to document and qualify on for mortgages or refinancing, and tax returns showing reduced early earnings could block or raise the cost of a future home move or loan.
